match.reason: The bank's calorimetry point teaches measuring heat from temperature change using q = mcΔT in chemistry reactions, not the three modes of heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) that the new point covers, so no bank point matches.

draft.title: Heat transfer
card: Heat is energy that moves from a hotter place to a cooler place. It moves in three ways: conduction, convection and radiation.
heat passing through direct contact. Vibrating particles pass energy to their neighbours without the material itself moving. Metals conduct well.
heat carried by the movement of a fluid, which is a liquid or a gas. Warmer fluid is less dense and rises, and cooler fluid sinks to replace it.
heat carried by electromagnetic waves, mainly infrared. It needs no particles, so it can cross empty space.
draft.remember: Conduction needs contact, convection needs a moving fluid, and radiation needs neither.

a.q: Which way of transferring heat can carry energy from the Sun to Earth through space?
a.why: Space is almost empty, so there are no particles to pass energy on or to flow as a fluid. Radiation uses electromagnetic waves, which need no particles. Conduction and convection both rely on particles.
a.clue: Which way does not need any particles?

b.q: Jin holds one end of a steel spoon. The other end sits in hot soup, and soon his hand feels warm. How did the heat mostly travel along the spoon?
opts: By conduction, as vibrating particles passed energy on
By convection, as hot steel moved up the spoon
By radiation, as waves crossed the air to his hand
By convection, as hot soup flowed along the handle
b.why: The spoon is a solid, so its particles stay in place and pass energy to their neighbours by vibrating. That is conduction. Convection is tempting because soup is hot, but it needs a fluid to move, and the steel does not flow.
b.clue: Does the steel itself move along the spoon?

b.best: By conduction, as vibrating particles passed energy on
